issue.title: sase stitch create's _stage_all_except swept a concurrent agent's uncommitted work into an unrelated commit, already pushed to origin/master
issue.description:
Reproduction in workspace sase_16 (host project gh_sase-org__sase) on 2026-08-13 while
implementing the approved plan
sase/repos/plans/202608/notification_read_current_tab.md. That plan's Python/test
changes were deliberately left uncommitted per the launching agent's instructions ("do
not create a git commit unless the user asks for one").

At 2026-08-13T18:42:15-0400 a commit appeared that this session never requested:

    commit aea9bf645a8e6e1fc7ccff57253f31068eb9f01a
    docs: add Grok Build coverage across provider documentation
    SASE_BEAD=[sase-l3.7]  SASE_TYPE=stitch  SASE_AGENT=[bbugyi200.athena.sase-l3.7]

`git show aea9bf645 --stat` shows its tree includes every file this session had changed
and left uncommitted for an unrelated bead (sase-l3.7, Grok Build docs):

    src/sase/ace/tui/modals/notification_modal.py
    src/sase/ace/tui/modals/notification_modal_action_types.py
    src/sase/ace/tui/modals/notification_modal_basic_actions.py
    src/sase/ace/tui/modals/notification_modal_constants.py
    src/sase/ace/tui/modals/notification_modal_tags.py
    src/sase/core/notification_store_wire.py
    src/sase/notifications/__init__.py
    src/sase/notifications/store.py
    tests/notification_store/test_state_updates.py
    tests/test_core_facade/test_notification_store.py
    tests/test_notification_modal_action_bindings.py
    tests/test_notification_modal_read_tab.py

`git show aea9bf645 -- src/sase/notifications/store.py` confirms the diff is the real
`mark_tab_read()` addition from the notification plan, not a coincidental docs-driven
touch. `git reflog show HEAD` shows this was a fresh `commit:` (not `commit (amend):`),
and the three neighboring commits from the same session window (d9c685e86, 4ff3a4161,
2e2facb94) are clean -- `git show <sha> --stat` for each has zero notification files --
so this is not routine amend misuse, it is a one-off cross-contamination between two
concurrent, unrelated agents sharing one git working tree.
`git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/master` returns true, confirming this
contaminated commit is already pushed/shared history on origin/master, not a local-only
mistake that can be quietly fixed.

Root cause: src/sase/vcs_provider/plugins/_git_commit_dispatch.py:140-147
(`_stage_all_except`) calls plain `git add -A` (repo-wide) whenever the commit payload's
`exclude` list is empty:

    def _stage_all_except(self, exclude: list[str], cwd: str) -> CommandOutput:
        """Stage every change, honoring `exclude` as literal pathspec excludes."""
        if not exclude:
            return self._run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd)
        ...

When a `sase stitch create`-driven commit runs in a workspace/working tree that another
agent is concurrently using for a *different*, still-uncommitted task, this stages and
commits that other agent's in-progress work too, silently. The resulting commit message
and SASE_BEAD trailer describe only the committing agent's own bead, so the bundled
changes are undiscoverable except by reading the actual diff.

Impact: (1) commit messages/trailers become inaccurate audit records; (2) unrelated work
streams get bundled into one pushed commit; (3) "do not commit unless the user asks"
gets silently violated whenever two agents race in a shared working tree, with no error
or warning to either agent. This session's launching agent was never told a commit
happened and only discovered it while investigating an unrelated just check-full
failure.

Not filing a remediation attempt here: fixing the notification-plan history (revert or
split the pushed commit) is a judgment call for the project owner given it is already on
origin/master, so that decision was left to the user in the same conversation instead of
being made unilaterally.

Suggested fix direction: scope `_stage_all_except`'s default (empty-exclude) path to the
files actually associated with the bead/stitch being committed (mirroring the
`exclude`-aware branch's use of pathspecs) instead of unconditional `git add -A`, or add
workspace-level isolation so concurrent SASE agents never share one git working tree for
uncommitted work.

evidence.note: IMPACT EVIDENCE from sase-ky.land (workspace sase_11, independent of the sase_16 report): the contaminated commit aea9bf645 leaves master RED at its own declared dependency floor. The swept-in half of the notification plan calls a core wire variant that does not exist in any sase-core release: 'just check' at HEAD 4183f3d4d with sase-core-rs 0.26.11 (the newest version satisfying pyproject's 'sase-core-rs>=0.26.10,<0.27.0') fails 6 tests -- tests/test_core_facade/test_notification_store.py::test_real_extension_mark_tab_read_scopes_to_one_tab and all 5 tests/notification_store/test_state_updates.py::TestMarkTabRead nodes -- with: ValueError: update is not a valid NotificationStateUpdateWire dict: unknown variant `mark_tab_read`, expected one of `mark_read`, `mark_all_read`, ... (src/sase/core/notification_store_facade.py:78). 'grep -rn mark_tab_read crates/' in the linked sase-core checkout at origin/master (v0.27.0) returns nothing, so the Rust side was never landed at all -- this is not a floor-ratchet problem like sase-lm, it is Python-only work that cannot pass at ANY core version. So the sweep did not merely mix unrelated changes into one commit; it published an incomplete feature that breaks the suite for every agent, and no revert-free core bump can fix it.
